title: Beef, Bean & Cheese Taco in Flour Tortilla

content.title: About
content.content: A taco is a Mexican dish consisting of a soft flour tortilla filled with seasoned beef, beans, and melted cheese. The tortilla is lightly toasted, while the filling combines juicy meat, creamy cheese, and hearty beans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flour tortillas are traditional in the northern regions of Mexico where wheat grows better than corn.
Beef for tacos is often seasoned with cumin, paprika, chili powder, and garlic for a distinctive flavor.
The beans used are usually black or pinto beans, providing a good source of protein and fiber.
Cheese in a classic taco is a melt‑friendly Mexican cheese such as cheddar or queso fresco.
Tacos are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and a squeeze of lime for brightness.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef and beans supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Beef provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Fiber from beans
items.content: Beans are rich in soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds minerals important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and the flour tortilla contain B12, B6, and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Beef and cheese can be high in saturated fats, so people with high cholesterol should enjoy tacos in moderation.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces often contain salt; those watching sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten in flour tortilla
items.content: Flour tortillas contain gluten, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tacos can be enjoyed hot or cold. Fold the tortilla in half and hold it in your hand. Add fresh salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or a squeeze of lime to taste. For a lighter version, use a whole‑grain tortilla.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared tacos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Keep tortillas and cheese separate to prevent sogginess. Frozen tortillas retain quality for up to 2 months.
